utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to assist me with Exhibit OTP 830 and 831.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Mr. DG, you have before you Exhibit 831, and on this telegram too do we see your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be kind enough to place the original on the ELMO again, please, page two, please, page two of the original. Now would you hand the telegram back to the witness, please, the original.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Mr. DG, on this telegram, it says that it was received on the 11th of July 1995 at 2350 hours. You said that the forward command post at Pribicevac, to which this telegram was addressed, was left by you between 1830 and 1930 hours. Can you explain how is it then that this time is indicated on this telegram? Before you answer that question, I should like to show you another exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit 830. Could it be given to the witness, please. With both exhibits in mind, could you please answer my question as to how it is possible for this telegram marked as OTP Exhibit 831 to have been received at 2350 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon arrival at Vlasenica, I -- it is my duty to carry my equipment and documents to the encryption office because they are -- may not be left in the vehicle. When I got there, the teleprinter operator and the encoder informed me that they had a telegram for me which they have to hand to me. I picked up the telegram from the teleprinter operator who handed it to me. I take over responsibility for it from him because it is his responsibility to hand it over to me.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Let us clear that up a little. You are saying that this telegram with the time indicated 2350 was received by you in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So this telegram with the time 2350 on it, that is, OTP Exhibit 830A, do you link this telegram to the telegram you have in front of you marked as OTP Exhibit 830 [as interpreted]. Will you please look at the stamp on it on page 2. Do you connect these two telegrams together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are one and the same telegram. The only thing being is one is outgoing and the other is incoming.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So is the outgoing the OTP 830 exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My co-counsel tells me that there is an error in line 17, page 59. It should say 831A instead of 830.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Mr. DG, could you give me a clear and specific answer, please. We have Exhibit 830 and the stamp on it indicating the time 2250, does that mean that somebody from Vlasenica, the encoder or the teleprinter operator received this telegram from his command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but he received it, the encoder received it at 2230.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And what about the time 2250, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means that he needed 20 minutes to process it, encode it, and hand it over to the teleprinter operator who would send it to me.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: After that time, that is, after 2250, does the teleprinter operator try to deliver it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, because that is his job.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But because he is unable to get into contact with me then, he put the telegram on the other side of the wall as one that has not been delivered.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So the moment you arrived in that room, he handed it over to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And then you entered this information with the time 2350.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. After which I took it to the operations centre and handed it to the officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Mr. DG, are you quite sure that you received this telegram in Vlasenica at 2350 in the way you have described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions for this witness, but I would like to briefly draw the attention of the Chamber to a problem which I assume Mr. Harmon will comment on. The problem occurred between the Defence and the Prosecution. In fact, the Defence notified the Prosecution what this witness would be testifying about, and in this notification, it omitted to mention some of the facts that the witness has testified to which was due to shortage of time and discussions that members of the Defence team had between Belgrade and The Hague. Mr. Harmon requested to postpone the cross-examination of this witness until tomorrow, which we fully agree with. I'm just informing Your Honours about it, and I assume that Mr. Harmon will also have something to say about it. But the Defence, as I have said, has finished with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm at the Chamber's disposal. I reviewed this summary, this factual summary. It is materially different than what the witness has testified to today, and I feel disadvantaged by virtue of that significant set of differences, particularly those found in the second paragraph of the summary. I am at your disposal. My preference would be to cross-examine this witness after I've had some time to reflect on now what is asserted to be an accurate statement of the facts, but I'm at your disposal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Harmon, we will act as follows: We will postpone the cross-examination of this witness for tomorrow. I hope there are no problems for the Defence -- for the witness, I'm sorry. So now is a good time for our lunch break. There's no point in beginning with another witness now, so we will now have our 50-minute lunch break, and we will come back to continue our work after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have in the courtroom before the Trial Chamber Witness DB, who testified on the 6th, 7th, and 8th of November last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness DB, we're going to refer to you in that way for reasons well known to you. You have already been here to testify. Let me remind you that we consider that you are still under oath because you took the solemn declaration when you first came to testify, so this is a continuation of that testimony, in fact. Having said that, Mr. Petrusic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, after the 12th of July 1995, you were at the forward command post of the Drina Corps, the forward command post of Krivace. During the time you spent at that forward command post, did you see Lieutenant Colonel Popovic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were you aware, did you have any knowledge or did you see Colonel Beara at the forward command post or perhaps in the region where the combat -- where combat took place in the period between the 12th of July and the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You testified in your examination-in-chief that on the 13th of July 1995 at the forward command post at Krivace, General Krstic arrived, as you said, some time in the morning hours before noon or around noon or in the early afternoon. You said you weren't able to remember correctly. Have I quoted you correctly, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, it would be helpful to me if Mr. Petrusic, when quoting previous testimony, could direct me to the page in the examination so I can check the examination and the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, do you know when General Krstic arrived at the Krivace forward command post, let me put it that way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, but there was the general question, the general issue. So please, when you quote somebody's testimony, could you please give us the page of the transcript so that the Prosecution can refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I accept your proposal and the objections made by the Prosecution and I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, do you know when General Krstic arrived at the Krivace command post, to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic arrived at the Krivace forward command post on the 13th of July, but I don't know whether it was exactly before noon or in the afternoon. I don't remember the time exactly but I do know that it was that particular date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From the 13th of July up until the 2nd of August, did General Krstic spend his days at the forward command post of Krivace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: During that time, did General Krstic tour the units that were engaged in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know where General Krstic spent the night, spent his nights during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic spent the night in the nearby village, a village several kilometres away from the forward command post. He was staying with his wife's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What was the communication means that General Krstic used during the time he spent at the Krivace forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: During his stay at the Krivace forward command post, for commanding subordinate units engaged in the Zepa operation, General Krstic used a radio device, the RU 2/2K with encryption protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was that the device that he used to communicate with the subordinate units who were engaged in combat at Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, the subordinate commanding officers, how did they address General Krstic, his subordinates, after his arrival at the Krivace forward command post? What was their form of address to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all addressed him according to the rules and regulations as "General, sir."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did anybody address him as "Commander"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, you were at the Pribicevac forward command post as well, were you not, which was established on the 5th of July and which remained operational until the 11th of July in the afternoon. During that time, during the time that the Pribicevac forward command post was in existence where General Krstic was present as well, who were or who was the driver of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, General Krstic had several drivers. One of them was his main driver; the other drivers accompanied the main driver. His main driver was a soldier, Dalibor Krstic, Private Dalibor Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That main driver, Dalibor Krstic, was he there from the 11th to -- 5th to the 11th, through that entire time, was he at the Pribicevac forward command post all the time during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was there throughout with General Krstic. I base that on the fact, my recollections on the fact that General Krstic in that period of time, because of his leg injury, had two or three times a day to bandage his wound. That is to say, he would have to care for his injured leg, and he was helped in doing that exclusively by his driver, Dalibor Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, at the Krivace forward command post, when did the units start arriving and the commanding officers of those units who were to engage in combat at Zepa? When did they start to arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the region of the forward command post of Krivace at Zepa, already on the 12th of July, the 5th Podrinje Infantry Brigade had already arrived, and it was commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Furtula. And the other units which took part in the operation at Srebrenica began to arrive in the regions where they were expected to be deployed at Zepa in the afternoon hours and in the early hours of the evening of the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the forward command post -- or let me ask you this: Do you know the commanding officer whose name was Miso Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the forward command post at Pribicevac between the 5th to the 11th, did you happen to see that particular commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did General Krstic use a vehicle with a radio telephone; that is to say, in the vehicle used by General Krstic, was there a radio telephone installed in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That particular device was a device that the Corps Commander's vehicle had, and I know that as a signalsman myself it was a problem, a great problem for me how I could reach General Krstic while he was resting for the night, because during that period of time he didn't take a signalsman with a mobile device with him, nor was there any other device in his car of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the night between the 11th and 12th of July after your arrival in Bratunac, did you on that occasion leave a signalsman behind with a device as an escort to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That particular device, who was General Krstic able to communicate with using that particular device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a mobile device within the network of command to the subordinate units who took part in the operation at Srebrenica. And using that device, he was able to communicate only with those units, only with the units who took part in the Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, when did you, yourself, arrive at the Krivace forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at the Krivace forward command post on the 12th of July early in the afternoon, immediately after noon, and I think it was at about 2.00 p.m. or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at Krivace, how much time did you need to make the device operational, the device which we call the teleprinter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions for this witness. We have completed our examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Harmon, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, good afternoon. I didn't think we'd be seeing each other so soon. Welcome back to The Hague. Witness, the first area you were examined by my colleague, you were asked the question whether you saw Lieutenant Colonel Popovic and Colonel Beara at the forward command post in Krivace, and your answer was that you did not see either one of them at the forward command post in Pribicevac. Did I understand your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at the forward command post of Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your testimony is not -- that they weren't in the Zepa area of responsibility from the 12th of July until the 2nd of August, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the lawyer, Mr. Petrusic, asked me the following question, he asked whether I had seen them during my stay at the Krivace forward command post and Godjenje forward command post in the area of combat operations during the Zepa operation, and I said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But your testimony to this Trial Chamber is not that these people weren't in the area where the Zepa operation was taking place, but that you personally didn't see them at the forward command post in Krivace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can testify that I did not see them at the forward command post in the Zepa region and that I did not hear that they were anywhere in the combat operation zone Zepa. So neither did I see them personally at the forward command post where I was, nor did I hear from anybody that they were somewhere in the zone where the combat operations were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Witness DB, during your previous examination, you testified that while you were in Zepa, a number of days after the operation started, you went back to your quarters in Vlasenica to the headquarters and you took a shower and a bath. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I returned for one night in the -- I came late at night and left early in the morning to return to the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is it possible, Witness DB, that in your absence, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic and/or Colonel Beara could have gone down to the Zepa area and been at the forward command post or within the area of responsibility in Zepa. Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Theoretically, that is possible, but I left the forward command post in the evening hours when all activities and combat operations were over for the day and returned in the early hours of the morning the following day. Now, if they were there in that period, I would have known that from my signalsman and I have no information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in addition to leaving the forward command post to go to take a bath up in Vlasenica, you also left the forward command post in the Zepa area to go visit your parents, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was towards the end of July, about the 25th, I would say. That is to say from the 25th to the 30th, and that was one afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did -- let me go into private session for just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us move into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How long a period of time did you stay at your parents'?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get to your parents'?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 45 minutes, between 45 minutes and one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: During that visit to your parents, did you stop any other place or did you go directly to your parents and return back to your post directly from your parents' house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I went straight back to the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Witness DB, is it possible that, in your absence, Colonel Beara came either to the forward command post or came to the Zepa area where combat operations and negotiations were being conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Theoretically, that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that theoretical possibility also refer to Lieutenant Colonel Popovic either coming to the forward command post or to the Zepa operation area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, but let me state once again, I have no knowledge about that in my absence because my signalsman would certainly have informed me about that, and then I wouldn't have testified the way I did, the way I am testifying, if that had been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's focus on your duties while you were at the forward command post, Witness DB. In fact, you were supposed to stay in and around the immediate area of the communications vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my basic task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in fact, you weren't supposed to leave that area in and around the communications centre of the forward command post, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I went, I went with the permission of my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many times during the Zepa operation, Witness DB, did you leave the forward command post area of the communications vehicle? Recall as best you can. You've already described two events: taking a bath in Vlasenica, visiting your parents. How many other times did you leave the immediate area of the forward command post during the whole Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my recollections, those were the only two times that I left for some considerable length of time. For the most part, I was -- that is to say, for the rest of the time I was within the region of the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, General Krstic left the area of the forward command post on a number of occasions, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Krstic, according to my knowledge, would go from time to time to the nearest units to see to the -- to directing the combat operations and to gain a personal insight into the problems that occurred on the front itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you didn't accompany him when he went on those journeys from the forward command post, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but a signalsman, a soldier, would always go with him with a mobile device.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you don't know who he met when he was away from the forward command post, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. My information is that he went to the commanding officers immediately subordinate in the area of the responsibility, and he would call me many times and tell me to convey a request of some kind with respect to more ammunition or some other materiel or logistics on another line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to read you some testimony of a witness who testified in open session with a pseudonym, referring to Witness DC.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And perhaps for the sake of this witness I could identify DC in private session so he knows who DC is. I think it's appropriate, given his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that would be a good idea. Let us move into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Witness DB, I'm going to read you the testimony of Witness DC. This was open session testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And counsel, for your convenience, I'm referring to page 7450, lines 4 through 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This was a question put to Witness DC by my colleague, Mr. Petrusic. Tell us, please, among the command staff of your Superior Command, did you see any of them at Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would see General Krstic most often. I also saw General Ratko Mladic. I saw some other senior officers from the Main Staff, as it was called then. Do I need to enumerate the names?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, tell us who you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Colonel Beara, Tolimir, officers from the Drina Corps who were with General Krstic, Colonel Vicic. Now, witness, I'm going to read you the testimony in open session that is in cross-examination. This is at page 7493, starting at line 2 and going to line 18. This was a question that I asked:

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see Colonel Popovic in Srebrenica on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say. I saw him somewhere. I did see him somewhere, whether it was Srebrenica or Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on a little bit in your testimony and ask you, you testified on direct examination about who you saw in Zepa, and in response to my colleague's question, you said you saw both General Krstic, General Mladic, and the Main Staff officers, including General Tolimir, Beara, and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did you see them in Zepa? Where was it that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them at the forward command post of Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Approximately when did you see Colonel Beara at the forward command post in Krivace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the operation, that was for sure, but I saw him several times. I think Beara or Tolimir, that they were negotiating with the Muslims. I don't know them very well, but I just saw them there. Now, let me go on to the next page. This was a re-examination question by my colleague Mr. Petrusic of the same witness, and this was in open session. It's on page 7503, lines 1 through 11. Witness DC, we heard from you today for the first time, and that is the first time I hear of it, too, that in the area of Zepa for a certain time, Colonel Beara was also present. Do you know what he was doing there? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present. I think he was involved in the negotiations, and he was also chief of security. I won't read the rest of the answer. I stopped at line 6. Now, let me turn to the last set of questions on this topic, Witness DB. This is found at page 7513, lines 17 through 25. Judge Wald asked Witness DC in open session: Witness DC, I have only two questions. Do you remember the date or approximately the time that Beara was in Zepa? I know you were there sometime from the 13th of July till the 2nd of August, I think. Can you place the time that he was there within that framework?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within that framework, the 13th, 14th, I didn't see him, but I think on the 15th onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you saw him several times from the 15th on when he was involved in negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now, Witness DB, do you have any reason to believe that Witness DC was not telling the truth before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Witness DC was one of the officers in one [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. That brigade had an axis of attack to the right, on the right flank. The forward command post of the Drina Corps was roughly in the middle, and to the far right along the axis of attack of other units and to the rear, as I learnt later, was the place where the negotiations were conducted with the Muslim forces from Zepa. So I cannot understand how Witness DC could have, as an officer who didn't have an important role, how [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. And the distance between them is 15 kilometres over mountainous terrain, and to see Colonel Beara who was at the negotiations. All I know is that in the forward command posts of Krivace and Godjenje and later Lovac too, two days later, that no negotiations were conducted at those forward command posts nor anywhere near those forward command posts. I learnt later on that those negotiations were conducted along the communication line between Zepa and Rogatica on the right flank, and this was at least 10 or 15 kilometres away from the forward command post. And if those persons were there, I wasn't there, so I can't tell, but I'm quite certain that where the negotiations were being held, Witness DC could not have been present because, at the time, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So Witness DB, [redacted] [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say -- I can't dispute [redacted] testimony. All I can do is maintain and stand behind my own testimony and everything else that I have just said. And my dilemma is -- the question is how [redacted] [redacted] away from the axis of attack of [redacted] unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You also said [redacted]. Did you see [redacted] there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see [redacted] at the forward command post of the Drina Corps at Krivace. [redacted] could have been at the forward command post of [redacted] own brigade, which was close by, maybe about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half away from the village of Godjenje where we had a second forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, did you know that General Tolimir was in the area of the Zepa operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was in the Zepa operation area and that he was at the location where the negotiations were going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him. I saw him on some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, was Miso Pelemis, who you've testified about, who you say you knew, was he in the Zepa area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that he wasn't at all in the Zepa area, neither he or his units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, can I have the witness please shown OTP Exhibit 881, please. If that could be distributed to counsel and to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness, take a moment to familiarise yourself with this article, if you would, please. There's a B/C/S version that's attached. Are you familiar, Witness DB, with the publication Drinski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does this appear to be an article from the Drinski magazine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it appears to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the Drinski magazine, would you tell the Judges, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I need to read the whole article? I haven't had time to read it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No. I'm going to direct your attention to a couple items in this article. Could you tell the Judges what the Drinski magazine is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drinski was a wartime magazine of the Zvornik Brigade which, in its editorial policies and programmes, to a good extent ignored the wartime reality of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, why don't you finish reading the article. It's not a very long article and if you -- and when you've finished that, just let me know and I'm going to ask you some questions about this article.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what I was asking you if I could do. Do I need to read the article on the second page?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I want you to be comfortable with the contents of this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: While the witness is reading that, if the usher could please prepare OTP Exhibit 28, Tab 15, please. If not, I have a copy that I could submit to the witness if it's not readily available. We can make my copy available to the witness when he's finished reading the article, that's fine. Madam Registrar, it's in this OTP 28, and the exhibit I'm specifically looking for is 28/17. 28/17 is on the back of the exhibit, but the grey tab number is 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Have you finished reading that article, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I apologise. It was rather difficult because the copy machine didn't copy the beginning of each word properly and clearly, so I had to use my common sense to guess what the words actually are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand. And it's my responsibility for furnishing you with a better copy. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could this exhibit be placed on the ELMO, Mr. Usher? This is a copy of 28/17, which is found in Prosecutor's Exhibit 28. If you place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness, this is an exhibit. It has been identified, and the people in this exhibit have been identified by previous witnesses, and this is a still image from a video that is also in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The video is, for Your Honours' -- for the record, Prosecutor's Exhibit 145 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the man on the far right-hand side of that particular still image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture is not clear and I'm not quite sure, but judging by the profile, it could be Miso Pelemis, Lieutenant Miso Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, leaving that exhibit right where it is, Mr. Usher, could you take the article that is in front of the witness and would you put the photograph, the top photograph next to the exhibit that is currently on the ELMO. If you would just kindly move the photograph of the man on the right a little to the left. Okay. Now, Witness -- no, a little bit more to the left, Mr. Usher, please. Now, would you move the black and white photograph closer to the image of the man in 28. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you see in the top picture of Prosecutor's Exhibit 881 the third man from the left, wearing a dark, darker-coloured outfit, who has a profile. Do you see that man I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you identify that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably would like me to say that they are one and the same person, but really, the photographs are so poor in quality that I can't say that, though the profiles are similar, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me pass to you, Witness DB, the original version of this magazine, and I'm going to ask you to study the same image, and I want your opinion on whether the individual, the two individuals are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Show it to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture is not much better, either. I must admit that these two profiles do look alike at first glance, but I wouldn't have the courage to ascertain that they were one and the same person with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, and for counsels' benefit, I have the original magazine, and if Your Honours would like to inspect it or counsel would like to inspect it, I can circulate that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Witness DB, let me move on just a little bit, and Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you pass that up to the Judges so they can look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, while we're on the topic of Miso Pelemis, you said you didn't see him at the forward command post in Pribicevac, but in fact, General Krstic on occasion could order Miso Pelemis to perform certain functions and tasks, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know - and that is what I testified the last time, I gave this same statement to the investigator, your investigator in April last year - I know that a unit of which Lieutenant Pelemis was the commander appeared somewhere in the area of combat operations over Srebrenica several days after those operations had started because as I was passing by not far from the Pribicevac forward command post, I saw their signalsman. And that prompted me, because I knew that they were not in the communications plan, so I was thinking forward as to how I would establish communications with them if they needed to hear a command from General Krstic, because we had a protected command line to subordinate units and that was the only line or connection that I recognised. So I sought to achieve that all units under the command of General Krstic should have a device, a coded device to be within the command network. However, their signalsman explained to me that they didn't need that device, and he continued along his way towards Srebrenica, probably where his unit was. In view of the fact that this was a diversionary detachment of the Main Staff which is not included in the plan for active combat activities but by purpose have special assignments, I came to the conclusion that this unit, which was very small in size and number, had some kind of a special assignment that was not a combat assignment. And until the end of that operation, we had no communication with them, nor do I have any knowledge that General Krstic had in any other way commanded that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, General Krstic knew Miso Pelemis, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just so the record is perfectly clear, Prosecution Exhibit 881, which is the article that you took a look at, is an article from Drinski magazine with a date of -- that the author gives to the text of the 24th of July 1995. This article -- take it, if you'd like to take a look at the original. This article deals with Zepa, doesn't it, and the operation in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The photograph could be from a much earlier period, from another period. Because in the footnote, it says Officer Svetozar Andric with associates. It doesn't indicate that it is in the operation for Zepa or anything like that. Secondly, it seems to me that Colonel Svetozar Andric had a black T-shirt on him, and here he is wearing a regular uniform. So this photograph may not have been taken from Zepa. It may have been taken out of the archives by the journalist as journalists are wont to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Svetozar Andric participated in the Zepa operation, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Last point of interest in this particular article is on the last page of this article in the last paragraph, full paragraph. It identifies General Krstic as the commander of the Drina Corps, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the journalist wrote here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's move on to again staying with the topic of Miso Pelemis. If the witness could please be shown Prosecution Exhibit 882. Witness, if you would turn over to the B/C/S version and review that. This, for your information, was an intercepted radio communication which has been dated the 25th of June 1995. Do you see the B/C/S version and could you read that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you put the English version on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review that intercepted communication, Witness DB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, I've managed to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the two correspondents in this intercepted communication are Popovic and General Krstic and midway down through this intercepted communication, I will read what is contained in it. Krstic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have reviewed this intercept briefly with my colleague, Mr. Petrusic. Could the Prosecutor explain briefly the purpose of showing him this conversation, because I don't think the witness has discussed the relationship between General Krstic and Pelemis and so on. So could Mr. Harmon explain, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The witness testified on direct examination that he had not seen Mr. Pelemis at the forward command post and this is relevant to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will read to you, Witness DB, what is said in this intercept and I'll start -- I'm starting midway through the intercept. Krstic: Have Miso Pelemis come over here with his unit as soon as possible. Popovic: Yes, sir. Krstic: So have him gather them urgently. Tell his lad that I asked him, because it's really much needed. We have big problems. Popovic: Yes, sir. Krstic: Do you understand? Popovic: Yes, sir. Now, Witness DB, there has been testimony in these proceedings, you first of all testified that you saw the 10th Sabotage Detachment communications officer at the forward command post at Pribicevac on the 9th of July and that you had a conversation with him. There has been the testimony of Drazen Erdemovic, who testified in public session, that his commander, during the Srebrenica operation, was Miso Pelemis. There has been video footage introduced in this trial, Prosecution Exhibit 145 bis, showing Miso Pelemis and General Mladic on the 11th of July 1995 in Srebrenica. So do you believe in light of, one, General Krstic's knowledge and familiarity with Miso Pelemis, this intercept, the evidence that I've just described of the presence of Miso Pelemis in Srebrenica, and the article from Drinski magazine that I showed you where the date is, I believe, the 24th of July. My first question that Miso Pelemis was present in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps during the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I think that I have given you an exhaustive answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: A detailed answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have another answer; it won't be exhaustive. Could I have a yes or no to the question that I have asked you. Do you believe that Miso Pelemis was in the Srebrenica area of responsibility on -- during the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence objects because we feel that the Prosecutor can ask the witness whether the Witness DB saw or has any knowledge or hearsay knowledge that Miso Pelemis was in Srebrenica but not in the way the question has been put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. I think that Mr. Harmon, having given a series of information to the witness, and as the witness was in the area, he is asking whether the witness believes what the Prosecutor is asking him. I think it's a legitimate question and the witness is going to answer it. Continue, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, can you answer my question or would you like me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember your question correctly, allow me to repeat my answer that I gave half an hour ago. I personally, at the Pribicevac forward command post, did not see Miso Pelemis. But from his signalsman and the shots that I saw here from Srebrenica on the 11th, I learnt that Miso Pelemis and his unit were there, but I personally did not see him. Nor did we - and I mean the command of the Drina Corps - did we have direct contact with Miso Pelemis and his unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you believe that Miso Pelemis, based on the information that I discussed with you, the article that I've shown you from the Drinski magazine, do you believe that Miso Pelemis participated in and was present in the Zepa area of responsibility during the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there is something I have to tell you. The document and the exhibit that you have shown me and which is in front of me now, I have to comment on it because I am a professional, and I have graduated from the highest military schools with respect to ways in which to collect material evidence of this kind, that is, intercepted communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, you can comment on the evidence in just a moment. The question I asked you is, do you believe that Miso Pelemis was present in the Zepa area of responsibility during the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I did not see his signalsman or Miso Pelemis, nor do I have any knowledge that Miso Pelemis himself or his unit were at Zepa. Therefore, in the area of Srebrenica, I did see his signalsman, and I knew from information that his unit was there. As for Zepa, neither did I have any knowledge that Miso Pelemis or his unit were there or his signalsman, nor did I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see it's 3.00. Are we going -- is this an appropriate time to break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much more time do you need, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Probably 15 more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Fifty?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fifteen, one five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Fifteen. [Interpretation] The idea was to finish with this witness today, but just a moment, please. I shall confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, is it possible for you to envisage now how much time you need for your additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That depends on the future questions from the Prosecution. I think we could be able to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let's try to finish with this witness today. So Mr. Harmon, please be as economical as you can with the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness, let me turn to another subject, which is related to your testimony, as to when you saw General Krstic at the forward command post in Krivace on the 13th of July. Now, previously you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you remember that interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember it in general terms. I probably don't remember it in all its details, but I remember what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in that interview, Mr. -- do you remember Jean-Rene Ruez, the investigator, the French investigator, asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: He asked you the following question: "Okay. So do you remember the 13th of July, at what moment of the day --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic. I apologise, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has not got the interview. Mr. Harmon is quoting a document. Would he please either rephrase the question or provide us with a copy of the text that he is quoting from and reading into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will be glad to. I hadn't finished phrasing the question before I was interrupted, but I was going to put the question then to the witness if he remembered the question and he gave that answer. So if I could be permitted, Mr. President, to read the question, I will then ask the question of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. And afterwards we'll see. We'll hear from Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, during the interview -- I'm going to read from the transcript of the interview: JEAN-RENE RUEZ Q. Okay, so do you remember 13th of July at what moment of the time did General Krstic arrive to Krivace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. He had the handover of duties in Drina Corps, so it was probably late in the evening, but I know for sure he wasn't there on the 12th, but he was there when the attack was launched. Witness DB, do you remember being asked that question and do you remember giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic, I assume you have no objection at this point in view of what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. But as a matter of principle, I would like to object to this method of asking questions. We feel that if Mr. Harmon is going to quote from a document, we ought to have the document too, and so should the witness to put himself into the context of what he is being asked, because we cannot assess the witness's answer because we can't assess what is said in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, your reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, the witness remembers the question and remembers the answer accurately. I believe that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could I have the witness then shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 364/1, 13 July 1995, tab 10. It's a document that is under seal, and if it's not readily available, I have a copy that I can make available to the witness immediately. Perhaps I will make my copy available, Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to speed matters up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is the B/C/S version. If you could show that to the witness, please. It's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please, if you'd read that intercepted communication. I'm referring to the bottom intercepted communication, Witness DB, the one that is intercepted off of the frequency 785.000. You can find it at the lower third of the page. Do you see that, channel 6, 1822 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what is the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The date of this is the 13th of July. The time of this intercept is 1822 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't know if Your Honours have this intercepted communication before Your Honours. It's difficult to examine without this, but I could read this into the record. It's under seal only because there are some initials that appear at the bottom. Can I read this into the record while the witness is reading this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is 785.000, I say this is the frequency, channel 6, 1822 hours. Participants, X - telephone switchboard (woman) C: He is out. X: What about Colonel Lazic? C: He is in the field. X: Is Lazic there? C: He is in the field. X: Is Krstic there? C: He is outside in front of the building. X: Tell him to come. The men can't wait. Night is falling. They have to work. The operation is at stake. C: He is here with General Mladic. X: Will you please, if it is possible, so that these men don't have to wait/? Tell them to/call on phone number 889-110. We are on (line?). C: Okay. X: Is it necessary to dial the area code 071? C: I know. X: Please. Take care. Thank you very much. C: You're welcome. Have a nice day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness DB, have you a chance to review this intercepted communication from the 13th of July at 1822 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was General Mladic at the forward command post on the 13th of July at 1822 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what about Colonel Lazic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who is Colonel Lazic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Lazic was an operations man in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And where was Colonel Lazic stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that he was in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where was he normally stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what period?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where he was exactly because at the time I had a lot of personal jobs -- I had a lot of jobs to attend to myself, and there was a lot of combat activity as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know where General Mladic was on the 13th of July at 1822 hours in the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. At the time, I was at the Krivace forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. We can conclude with this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I something, Mr. Prosecutor? May I be allowed to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I am trying to get through this examination quickly. You will have an opportunity with Mr. Petrusic asking you questions but, please, if you have a comment about this document, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can comment this document only on the assumption that it is correct and authentic, on that assumption alone. Because I was in a position to look through some other documents where two intercepting groups from different positions were intercepting and recording certain conversations and there was so many differences and mistakes and things that were not clear in them that, for example, because of poor audibility and because of the people that were doing the intercepting because they were poorly trained and not professional enough, I remember one of them writing down a report saying, "It's all right we're still fighting," whereas the other one from the other post was saying, "It's all right, we'll be hearing from each other." So these are words that in our language sound very similar. Their sound is similar but of course they mean something quite different. And I can quote many such examples. So this is just my comment with respect to these documents and, therefore, I can only comment this particular document on the assumption that what it says here is a true copy, an authentic copy of the conversation recorded. Only on that assumption. I say this purely from the aspects of my profession. My professional training in the army allows me to make that comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, you said that you left the forward command post on the 12th of July -- I'm sorry, the evening of the -- you left the forward command post on the 12th of July -- I'm sorry, the 11th of July, the evening of the 11th of July. Now, when you packed up your radio communications van, did you tell the headquarters at the Vlasenica that you were packing up and were going to be off of the communications net?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember exactly. I don't remember that detail whether I called them and told them or whether I just packed up and left. I don't remember that particular detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, let's stay with military logic for a moment, Witness DB. The communications centre at the forward command post in Pribicevac was the central, critical communications post on the net; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was an important link in the command chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So is it logical, in the military sense, that the important nerve centre, communications nerve centre of the operation would be unplugged and nobody would be told at the operations headquarters at Vlasenica that you were going off line? Could you comment on that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right from the theoretical standpoint. But from Pribicevac to the first major communications point network in Bratunac, I needed about an hour, a maximum of an hour so that as the combat positions changed and the units and the command moved forward, it was essential that a soldier carrying a mobile device go with General Krstic and that he command the units at Srebrenica. So that was the main goal, the main objective and that line remained continuous. But my move to Bratunac and this interruption of one hour at that particular point in time, it was not serious, a serious break in communications because we planned that communications centres should move around. Whether I told Vlasenica or not that we would be moving, I really can't say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, you were out of communications links for about four hours, by my calculation, Witness DB. What do you think you did? Did you tell Vlasenica headquarters that you were going out of the net for about four hours? What do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: My main job was that I was near to General Zivanovic and near to General Krstic. That was the main thing for me. And it was up to them. They decided everything and they were in command. So me and my connections were there to serve them, whereas the Vlasenica did not interest me any more. There was nobody there in Vlasenica to make key decisions with respect to the Krivaja 95 operation. All the officers taking decisions in the Krivaja 95 operation were close by, close to me in the broader Srebrenica area and I was able to reach them. So it wasn't essential for me to maintain lines with Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was your normal practice when you moved, when you packed up a forward communications centre and moved? Was your normal practice to inform the headquarters that you were doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those headquarters, as I said, those -- the decision-makers in the Krivaja 95 operation were there close by me in the area of responsibility and the broader region of Srebrenica. So the reason why I had come to Srebrenica which was to help the command of the Srebrenica operation, that line was not interrupted and that was what was important for me. And let me say again, perhaps I did call Vlasenica purely for technical reasons as a go-between and maybe I didn't. I don't remember. I don't remember that particular detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. My question was something different. What was your normal practice when you pulled up a forward command post communications centre and left and went off the line? Did you normally contact the headquarters and tell them that you were now no -- you were blacked out, you were no longer capable of being communicated with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say again, if the command, if all those in command of the Srebrenica operation, or rather Krivaja 95, had they been in Vlasenica, then it would have certainly been my job to call them. That is the rule. But as I say, they were all in the Srebrenica region.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So in the VRS, Witness DB, it is militarily acceptable for a forward command post communications centre to go out of the communication net without informing the headquarters of the corps or those in superior command; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you said that, Mr. Prosecutor. I am trying to explain to you the practice and what we do in the field, practical steps, wartime steps. So my command was in the broader region of Srebrenica which meant that both General Krstic and General Zivanovic were there. And they, for me, are the command, the commanding officers. And they are the ones requiring those lines. Vlasenica, at that point in time, was just a go-between for other communication lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We'll move on to a different topic. Who were the other drivers for General Krstic? You mentioned one; could you tell me who the others were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, of General Krstic's drivers, I remember that there was Dalibor Tosic who, later on, was given another assignment during the operation on Zepa and he was seriously wounded so I link these events up. There was another driver from Vlasenica and his name was Bjelanovic. He came later on, but during those operations, he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, I apologise for interrupting. I know that you did your best to wind up but I think we have reached our limits and we can't overstep that limit. Let me therefore propose that we hear the end of this testimony tomorrow. Witness DB, you will have to come back tomorrow because I'm afraid we cannot continue now. So we're going to adjourn for the day and we reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.20 to hear the rest of your testimony. I apologise Mr. Harmon, but this is a time constraint that we're facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I apologise I couldn't finish as fast as I wanted but, Your Honour, I have one question and I realise there is a rule about contact with witnesses but I notice that there has been a witness, an expert witness who has been in the audience during the course of DB's testimony, and there is a no-contact rule with this in -- that has been in practice. I know my colleagues from the Defence intend to abide by that but I would ask that the witness who has been in the audience also be admonished not to have contact with this witness overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness in the public gallery will be next to testify; is that right, Mr. Harmon? Is that the basis for what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic or Mr. Petrusic, would you like to respond? Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the proposal is in order and we, of course, did intend to adhere to that rule and the witnesses are not located -- have not -- do not have the same accommodation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Visnjic. We have full confidence in you and we hope that everything will develop properly and in order and we adjourn the meeting until tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
